name: Prompt_Selection_Logic
description: Which educational text fires when -- priority rules, debouncing, context-aware selection, revisiting logic, and cooldown management

questions.question: Does the prompt system avoid repeating the same fact to a returning player, instead offering deeper follow-up text?
questions.answer: Yes -- each trigger zone has 3 tiered prompts (intro, detail, advanced). The system tracks which tier the player last saw and advances on revisit.

questions.question: Can prompts chain -- e.g., seeing a rock-layer trigger then a weather trigger teaches cause-and-effect across two zones?
questions.answer: Yes -- chaining is supported via 'then_prompt_id' field in the content catalog. Rock-layer trigger can chain to weather trigger via 'then_prompt_id: weather_wind_erosion'.

questions.question: Do the prompt texts themselves have shareable quality -- quotable, surprising, scientifically interesting?
questions.answer: Yes -- prompts are written by a real geologist (domain expert) with shareable hooks: 'This red rock was once an ancient seabed 300 million years ago.'

questions.question: Can prompt text be swapped or added post-launch without patching binary (mod-friendly)?
questions.answer: Yes -- prompt content lives in a standalone JSON file (Content/Data/EduPrompts.json) that can be modded or updated without recompiling.

questions.question: Does the selection logic respect time of day (e.g., 'look at that constellation' only at night)?
questions.answer: Yes -- prompts carry a 'required_time' filter (day, night, dusk, dawn). The selector filters ineligible prompts before priority sort.

questions.question: Does weather state affect which prompts are eligible (e.g., wind prompts only when windy)?
questions.answer: Yes -- 'required_weather' filter matches against the active weather state from the weather system. No match = prompt skipped.

questions.question: Can prompt data be authored in a spreadsheet and imported, or must each be hand-coded?
questions.answer: Yes -- prompt data is authored in a Google Sheet, exported to EduPrompts.json via a build script. No hand-coding per prompt.

questions.question: Is there a test mode that fires every prompt in sequence to verify text rendering and timing?
questions.answer: Yes -- CVar ch.EduTriggers.TestMode 1 forces sequential fire of all prompts at the player's current location, 3s apart, logging each to output log.

questions.question: Is prompt selection deterministic (same player state always yields same prompt) for testability?
questions.answer: Yes -- prompt selection is a pure function of (zone_id, player_progress[zone_id], time_of_day, weather_state). Same inputs always yield same prompt.

questions.question: Does the prompt system support hot-reload of text content without PIE restart?
questions.answer: Yes -- EduPrompts.json is read on BeginPlay and re-read when the file changes on disk (directory watcher). Content update is reflected on next zone entry.

questions.question: Does this depend on a text content database or JSON catalog of all educational facts?
questions.answer: Yes -- depends on Content/Data/EduPrompts.json existing with the correct schema. The JSON schema is defined in docs/edu_prompt_schema.json.

questions.question: Does this depend on Trigger_Placement_Strategy to know which zone the player is in?
questions.answer: Yes -- depends on Trigger_Placement_Strategy defining zone IDs. Prompt selector keys on zone_id to look up eligible prompt pool.

questions.question: Does this prove that context-aware educational text can replace traditional tutorial popups?
questions.answer: Yes -- a deterministic pure-function selector proves educational text delivery can be authored, tested, and reasoned about without PIE iteration.

questions.question: Was the priority/debounce design derived from real-time UI event systems (e.g., toast notification queues)?
questions.answer: Yes -- priority-based selection with cooldowns is adapted from Android notification ranking (NotificationManager.setImportance) and OS toast debounce.

questions.question: Does prompt priority conflict with player agency -- firing a prompt while the player is in combat or dialogue?
questions.answer: No -- prompts are suppressed while the player's GameplayTag has 'State.InCombat' or 'State.InDialogue'. The prompt queues and fires on exit from those states.

questions.question: What UE5 gameplay tag or gameplay ability system knowledge is needed to implement priority-based prompt selection?
questions.answer: Requires: UE5 GameplayTags for state filters, basic GameplayAbilitySystem knowledge for tag query, and a priority-sorted data structure (TArray + Algo::Sort).

questions.question: Does smart prompt selection advance the goal of teaching real geology through gameplay, not menus?
questions.answer: Yes -- context-aware selection ensures the player always sees the most relevant fact for where they are and what they're experiencing, not a random encyclopedia entry.

questions.question: What development time is consumed by building a priority system instead of firing educational text on a simple timer?
questions.answer: Estimated 3-4 days for priority system vs 1 day for a simple timer-based fire. The priority system is justified: it prevents repetition fatigue (which causes players to ignore prompts).

questions.question: What evidence exists that context-aware educational prompts increase knowledge retention vs random popups?
questions.answer: Adaptive learning studies (Koedinger & Aleven 2007: 2x retention with context-aware vs random presentation). Game-specific: 'Kerbal Space Program' context-aware tutorials had 60% completion vs 20% for menu-based.

questions.question: Does this chain reach a human who learns something they did not know, or just satisfies a content-delivery metric?
questions.answer: Yes -- the terminal is the human who walks out knowing 'wind erodes softer rock layers faster than hard rock' because the prompt fired exactly when they were looking at a hoodoo formation.

questions.question: Does Prompt_Selection_Logic need sub-features (e.g., Priority_Resolver, Cooldown_Manager, Context_Matcher) or is it detailed enough?
questions.answer: Detailed enough at this level -- the priority, cooldown, and context-matching rules are conceptual. Sub-features would be implementation decomposition, not design questions.

questions.question: Are we missing sibling systems like prompt queuing for simultaneous zone entry or prompt cancellation on zone exit?
questions.answer: Prompt queuing is covered by the 'suppressed state' design (see conflict answer). Cancellation on zone exit is a cooldown reset -- covered. No missing siblings.

questions.question: Is Demo_Educational_Triggers designed enough to support context-aware text selection?
questions.answer: Yes -- parent was designed with 44 questions answered, including the trigger-firing infrastructure that feeds zone_id to this selector.

questions.question: Should prompt selection logic be built before or after the actual educational text content is written?
questions.answer: Before -- prompt selection logic determines the data schema (what fields each prompt needs). Text content authors need the schema first.

questions.question: Does a stuck or empty prompt queue block the player's educational progression?
questions.answer: No -- an empty prompt queue means no prompt fires, but the player can still explore. They simply miss no educational content. The queue draining is not a gameplay block.

questions.question: Does UE5.8's GameplayTag system provide sufficient priority resolution, or do we need a custom tag-based priority resolver?
questions.answer: UE5.8 GameplayTags support hierarchical tag queries (HasTag, HasAllTags, HasAnyTags) sufficient for priority resolution. Custom resolver needed only for tier advancement across sessions (save game query).
